citation.title: Transformer-based Topology Optimization
citation.authors: Aaron Lutheran; Srijan Das; Alireza Tabarraei

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For 64 × 64 static cases, the transformer sampled designs in roughly 2 seconds versus 66 seconds for classical topology optimization, a 33-fold speedup with 1.88% mean compliance error.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Section 5 explicitly reports 33×; 66 s classical / 2 s model = 33.
claim.alternatives: Same Section 5 paragraph gives dynamic speedup of 4,450× (8,900 s versus 2 s) with 4.81% compliance error. Table 2 earlier reports static quality metrics relative to classical-generated ground truth.

baseline.classical_method: Conventional iterative SIMP-style topology optimization, with static and dynamic formulations (Sections 2 and 4.1)
baseline.classical_iterations: convergence by relative compliance change or iteration limit described generically in Section 2; actual benchmark stopping rule not stated
baseline.classical_time: 66 s static and 8,900 s dynamic on average (Section 5)
baseline.ml_time: roughly 2 s per sample, static and dynamic (Section 5)
baseline.training_time: 800,000 training iterations per model, batch size 256 (Section 5); wall-clock not stated
baseline.data_generation_cost: 60,000 static optimization samples and roughly 6,000 dynamic samples (Sections 4.1 and 4.4); generation time not stated
baseline.quality_metric: FE compliance error, target volume fraction error, load discrepancy, floating material percentage, and proportion above 30% compliance error (Section 5, Tables 2–3)
baseline.quality_gap: static ViT-Small mean compliance error 1.88% and volume fraction error 1.01% (Table 2); dynamic decoder-layers model 4.81% compliance error and 4.38% volume fraction error (Table 3)

R1.evidence: Section 5 and Tables 2–3: the speed comparisons use full classical runs but return designs with nonzero compliance and volume error, with no quality or time matching.

R2.evidence: Sections 4–5: implementation, solver, hardware and iteration timings for the classical benchmark are absent, so no R2 failure criterion can be established from the text.

R3.evidence: Sections 4.1, 4.4 and 5: tens of thousands of optimizer-generated training samples and 800,000 training iterations are reported, but neither data-generation nor training wall-clock cost nor break-even use count is given.

R4.evidence: Section 5, Tables 2–3: compliance on generated designs is compared with optimized ground truth, and volume error, floating material, and the proportion above 30% compliance error are counted for held-out cases.

notes: Latest arXiv v2 full text. The model requires an initial FE analysis to construct stress and strain inputs (Section 4.1, Figure 1); the 2 s model timing is called sampling time, with no statement that input FE preprocessing is included. Table 3 reports 48.0% floating material for the best dynamic model.
